Timeline::is_scalar¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

bool Timeline::is_scalar() const

What It Tells You¶

is_scalar() is the readable form of dim() == 0. It answers whether the timeline represents one unindexed instant rather than an array with axes.

This distinction is important for scalar-only operations such as isoformat(), scalar bounds passed to range builders, and APIs that require exactly one instant rather than merely one stored position.

A shape [1] timeline also contains one position, but it is a vector and therefore returns false. Cardinality and scalar structure must not be used interchangeably.

Returns¶

true exactly when the logical rank is zero.

Examples¶

Example 1. Contrast a scalar with a one-element vector.

auto scalar = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:30:00Z");
auto singleton = pluss::timeline::make({"2024-02-29T12:30:00Z"});

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "scalar: numel=" << scalar.numel()
          << ", is_scalar=" << scalar.is_scalar() << "\n"
          << "singleton: numel=" << singleton.numel()
          << ", is_scalar=" << singleton.is_scalar() << "\n";

Output¶

scalar: numel=1, is_scalar=true
singleton: numel=1, is_scalar=false

Example 2. Guard a scalar-only formatter at an API boundary.

auto render_one = [](const pluss::Timeline& value) {
    if (!value.is_scalar()) {
        return std::string{"expected one scalar instant"};
    }
    return value.isoformat();
};

auto scalar = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:30:00Z");
auto vector = pluss::timeline::make({"2024-02-29T12:30:00Z"});
std::cout << render_one(scalar) << "\n" << render_one(vector) << "\n";

Output¶

2024-02-29T12:30:00.000000000+00:00
expected one scalar instant

Example 3. host() has a deliberately different decision rule: it condenses any one-position timeline to its scalar host payload.

auto singleton = pluss::timeline::make({"2024-02-29T12:30:00Z"});
auto host = singleton.host();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "dim=" << singleton.dim()
          << ", is_scalar=" << singleton.is_scalar()
          << ", host scalar=" << host.is_scalar() << "\n";

Output¶

dim=1, is_scalar=false, host scalar=true

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Do not replace this test with numel() == 1 when an API requires rank zero.

  • is_scalar() says nothing about validity of the timestamp; a scalar may hold NaT.

  • host().is_scalar() describes the selected host payload variant, not the original timeline’s rank.
